editorial.description_en: Marsh water in shadow, where the yellow-green survives the loss of light better than the blue-greens do.
editorial.description_ja: 影になった沼のような、暗い黄緑。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.360, C 0.050, h 128.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 沼 (numa, marsh) + 影 (kage, shadow). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Marsh Shadow" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 沼影. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — rin-sho at ΔE00 6.2, fuyu-sugi at ΔE00 7.6, tetsu-midori at ΔE00 8.8. complementary is empty because no entry in this corpus sits within 22° of the opposite hue. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
